public_rationale: The ordinary contemporary reading is supported. OpenAI reports nonzero hallucination rates, and Google documents errors even with retrieved context. Retrieval and abstention can reduce risk, but the cited evaluations do not show its elimination. This does not establish that all conceivable chatbots must hallucinate forever.
limitations: The conclusion depends on reading chatbot in the post's general-purpose generative-AI context.
Benchmark error rates are not representative estimates for every deployment.
The sources report capabilities during the target quarter; exact underlying test dates are not supplied in the cited passages.

statement.document_title: Generative AI’s crippling and widespread failure to induce robust models of the world

our_interpretation: The plain reading concerns general-purpose generative chatbots available when Marcus wrote: factual fabrication remains a possibility, including with retrieval.
Always a risk does not mean every answer is wrong or establish an immutable limit on every future chatbot.
Because no reporting period is specified, use the current calendar quarter through publication, April 1–June 28, 2025.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations document factual hallucinations in general-purpose chatbot models, including systems supplied with retrieved information.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad, credible evaluations establish that contemporary general-purpose chatbots reliably eliminate factual fabrication across their intended uses, including difficult questions and incomplete retrieved information.

evidence.excerpt: The o4-mini model underperforms o1 and o3 on our PersonQA evaluation.
evidence.explanation: The April system card reports PersonQA hallucination rates of 33% for o3 and 48% for o4-mini, establishing residual factual-error risk. These are benchmark results, not estimates of the proportion of ordinary chatbot conversations containing hallucinations.

evidence.locator: Introduction, paragraph beginning A main challenge; Key insights into RAG systems
evidence.explanation: Google's researchers describe residual hallucinations in retrieval-augmented systems, including failures by Gemini, GPT and Claude when context is insufficient. They also report that sufficient context and selective abstention improve performance, which limits the claim to persistent risk rather than inevitable failure.
